turn.text: "How much swap and zram do I have, how much of it is in use right now, and is my RAM under pressure?"

content.text: Run read-only commands to check swap/zram and memory pressure.
I'll check your swap, zram and memory state directly.

input.command: swapon --show; echo ---; free -h; echo ---; zramctl; echo ---; cat /proc/pressure/memory 2>/dev/null; echo ---; echo vm.swappiness=$(cat /proc/sys/vm/swappiness)

content.text:
NAME       TYPE      SIZE USED PRIO
/swapfile  file        8G   0B   10
/dev/zram0 partition 7.6G 1.3G  100
---
               total        used        free      shared  buff/cache   available
Mem:           7.6Gi       6.4Gi       298Mi       129Mi       1.6Gi       1.2Gi
Swap:           15Gi       1.3Gi        14Gi
---
NAME       ALGORITHM DISKSIZE DATA  COMPR  TOTAL STREAMS MOUNTPOINT
/dev/zram0 zstd          7.6G 1.2G 290.6M 303.1M         [SWAP]
---
some avg10=0.00 avg60=0.06 avg300=0.12 total=12797537
full avg10=0.00 avg60=0.02 avg300=0.09 total=11584802
---
vm.swappiness=150

Interpret: swapfile 8G with 0 used, zram 7.6G with 1.3G used (compresses 1.2G data down to ~303M physical RAM). Total swap 15G. RAM: 7.6G total, 6.4G used, 1.2G available. PSI: some avg10=0, avg60=0.06 — negligible pressure. So no real pressure; zram doing its job well (4x compression).

You have **15 GiB of swap total: 7.6 GiB zram + 8 GiB swapfile — and RAM is not under real pressure right now.**

## What's there and in use

| Device | Size | Used now |
|---|---|---|
| zram (in-RAM, zstd) | 7.6 GiB | 1.3 GiB |
| /swapfile (disk) | 8 GiB | 0 B |

The zram is working well: it's holding 1.2 GiB of data compressed down to about 303 MiB of actual RAM — roughly 4× compression, so it's saving you ~900 MiB that the disk swap never had to touch.

## Memory pressure: essentially none

- **PSI (pressure stall info):** `some avg10=0.00, avg60=0.06, avg300=0.12` — near zero over the last 10 seconds to 5 minutes. Processes are not being stalled waiting for memory.
- **free:** 6.4 GiB of 7.6 GiB used, but only 1.2 GiB of that is "unavailable" — `available` (what apps can actually still grab) is 1.2 GiB, which is comfortable.
- **Swappiness is 150**, tuned for zram, so the system prefers moving cold pages into compressed zram over hitting the disk file — matches what you see (disk swap untouched).

Nothing to fix. The zram is doing its job and everything currently paged out lives in fast compressed RAM, not on your disk.
